f63503e330: <0>How miners are counted.</0> The chain knows payout addresses, not people or computers. "Mining addresses" are the distinct addresses credited with at least one share in the last 360 blocks (about 6 hours); over 24 hours more addresses appear, because not everyone mines all day. One address may pay for many computers, and one person may use several addresses, so the number of machines is not known to anyone. The hashrate is measured from the shares every block credits (about 32 per block), and GPU equivalents divide it by one RTX 5090 (about 74 MH/s).
